nodes.prompt:
Check this change for DESIGN DRIFT. This is a check: do NOT edit
anything, and do NOT judge whether a deviation is justified — report
it, and leave the judging to others.

1. Read the design document `{{ inputs.design }}` in full.
2. Read the change: `git diff {{ inputs.base }}..{{ inputs.head }}`, then
   every changed file as it stands at `{{ inputs.head }}`.
3. List EVERY place where the code does something the design does not
   say, or does not do what the design says. That includes silently
   narrowing a rule the design states (a check that admits less than
   the design promises) and silently widening one (a check that admits
   more).
4. For each item, find the commit that introduced it: use `git log`
   and `git blame` over `{{ inputs.base }}..{{ inputs.head }}`.

Finish the check BEFORE you reply. Your FINAL reply IS the verdict: the
node's turn ends the moment you reply, so a file you promise to read
afterwards is never read. START the reply with exactly one of these two
bare tokens, as the very FIRST characters, with no markdown emphasis
(`**NO_DRIFT**` and `**DRIFT:**` are WRONG), no heading, no preamble:
  - NO_DRIFT — you held the whole change against the design and found
    nothing.
  - DRIFT: — followed by ONE fenced ```json array, one object per item:
      {"id": "D1", "clause": "<the design text, quoted>",
       "expected": "<what the design says>",
       "actual": "<what the code does>",
       "evidence": "<path:line>",
       "commit": "<short sha>", "subject": "<commit subject>"}
    Number the ids D1, D2, … in the order you list them.
Anything you need to qualify goes AFTER the verdict, never before it: a
line of context ahead of the token fails this node even when the check
is finished.

A drift check held a change against the design document
`{{ inputs.design }}` and reported this:
{{ artifacts.drift/check | inline }}

If that report is NO_DRIFT, there is nothing to answer: reply with the
bare token NO_DRIFT and stop.

Otherwise, for EACH item in its JSON list, speak for the author of the
commit it names. Read `git show <commit>` — the diff AND the message —
and whatever else that author would have had in front of them. Then
answer, as that author would:
  - why the code differs from the quoted clause;
  - whether the author holds that the DESIGN is right (the code should
    change) or the CODE is right (the design is out of date, or the
    deviation is deliberate).
Argue the author's case from what the commit and the code show; where
they show nothing, say so rather than inventing a reason. This is an
interview: do NOT rule on any item, and do NOT edit anything.

Finish BEFORE you reply. Your FINAL reply IS the verdict. START it with
exactly one of these two bare tokens, as the very FIRST characters, with
no markdown emphasis (`**INTERVIEWED:**` is WRONG), no heading, no
preamble:
  - NO_DRIFT — the report was NO_DRIFT.
  - INTERVIEWED: — followed by ONE fenced ```json array, one object per
    item: {"id": "<the item's id>", "why": "<the author's account>",
    "holds": "design" or "code", "evidence": "<path:line or sha>"}.
Anything you need to qualify goes AFTER the verdict, never before it: a
line of context ahead of the token fails this node even when the
interview is finished.

Rule on a drift report. The design document is
`{{ inputs.design }}`. The drift check reported:
{{ artifacts.drift/check | inline }}

The authors' side, from an interview that read their commits:
{{ artifacts.nego/interview | inline }}

If the report is NO_DRIFT, reply with the bare token NO_DRIFT and stop.

Otherwise read the design and the code yourself, weigh both sides, and
give EVERY item exactly one outcome:
  - fix-code — the design is right; the code must change to match it.
  - amend-design — the code is right and the design must change. That
    is a person's call: it stops this run for a human.
  - accept-deviation — the code may differ from the design as it is;
    say why in the reason.
This is a ruling: do NOT edit anything, and do NOT fix anything.

Finish BEFORE you reply. Your FINAL reply IS the verdict. START it with
exactly one of these three bare tokens, as the very FIRST characters,
with no markdown emphasis (`**RESOLVED:**` is WRONG), no heading, no
preamble:
  - NO_DRIFT — the report was NO_DRIFT.
  - RESOLVED: — no item is amend-design. Follow it with ONE fenced
    ```json array, one object per item:
    {"id": "<the item's id>", "outcome": "fix-code" or
    "accept-deviation", "reason": "<why>"}.
  - AMEND_DESIGN: — at least one item is amend-design. Follow it with
    the same JSON array, every item included.
Anything you need to qualify goes AFTER the verdict, never before it: a
line of context ahead of the token fails this node even when the ruling
is finished.

Apply this drift ruling:
{{ artifacts.nego/rule | inline }}

If the ruling is NO_DRIFT, or it has no fix-code item, change nothing:
reply with the bare word PASS and stop.

Otherwise make the code match the design document
`{{ inputs.design }}` for EVERY fix-code item, and ONLY those. Leave
accept-deviation items exactly as they are. This is a fix round: do
NOT re-rule any item, and do NOT edit the design.
Your grant is exactly this: Read, Grep, Glob, Edit, Write, and two
programs through Bash, `git` and `make`. Any other call is denied, not
asked about. So:
  - run the tests with `make`. The command the engine runs as your
    evidence is `{{ inputs.verify }}`, so run exactly that;
  - commit with `git commit -m '<subject>' -m '<body>'`, adding the
    trailer `Co-Authored-By: oh-my-graph <graphs@oh-my-graph.dev>`
    as one more `-m` (the attribution convention in CONTRIBUTING.md),
    and keep each `-m` on one line;
  - every Bash call is ONE program: no `cd`, `&&`, `;`, `|`, redirect
    or heredoc. To act in another directory, use `git -C <dir>` or
    `make -C <dir>`;
  - a denied call means the FORM was wrong, not the goal: re-issue it
    in one of the forms above before you give up on it.
Commit as you go, every commit carrying that trailer. Run the tests
SYNCHRONOUSLY and wait for them to finish — never in the background.
Your FINAL reply is the verdict: never end the turn on an interim
report. When tests are green, START the reply with the bare word PASS —
those four characters FIRST, no markdown emphasis (`**PASS**` is
WRONG), no heading, no preamble. Otherwise start it with a bare FAIL
and what is broken. Anything you need to qualify goes AFTER the
verdict, never before it: a line of context ahead of the token fails
this node even when the tests are green.
